result.narrative:
Boeing sits in the Watch band at a score of 27.8, driven almost entirely by negative news flow rather than any payment deterioration. Payment behaviour is clean - no open overdues and a single historical late payment that resolved quickly - so the 0.65 payment leg of the score contributes nothing to the elevated reading. The 0.35 news leg carries the full 27.8 points, reflecting a credible, multiply-corroborated pattern of commercial-aircraft production stress: a 5% commercial workforce cut (reported independently by Reuters, CNBC, NYT and WSJ), a 14% October delivery drop, a 737 MAX production-ramp delay to 2027, and weaker free-cash-flow guidance, alongside continued positive commercial news (record $745B backlog, $20B Navy contract, prospective 250-plane China order).

The band is set by the severity-4 "leaves open possibility of more layoffs" headline, which is the most recent and highest-weighted article; the adjudicator agrees with the Watch classification but flags that this specific headline is a single, body-less Reuters story not independently corroborated, even though the broader layoff trend it extends is well-attested elsewhere. The adjudicator also notes the clean payment record rests on thin history - one notification, one insurer (TCI) - limiting confidence that it reflects a durable trend. Neither point is grounds to dispute the band, but both warrant underwriter attention.

The recommended action is to maintain the current $9,000,000 limit with TCI unchanged (owed $0), as PD of 0.1784 remains within the 0.25 appetite threshold and expected loss is unchanged before and after.

A move to the lower Healthy band would need the score to fall by 7.8 points, which would likely follow as the layoff/production-stress news ages and decays (half-life 365 days) without fresh negative coverage, or the Reuters follow-on report being corroborated as isolated rather than part of an escalating pattern.

judgement.bottom_line: Maintain the $9,000,000 limit with TCI; the Watch band is appropriate but the adjudicator flagged caveats - the driving headline is single-sourced and the clean payment record rests on thin history - so treat as agree-with-caveats rather than a clean pass.
judgement.payment_note: Payment history shows no open overdues and only one resolved late payment (TCI, $650k, 3 days late), with insufficient history to establish a firm trend.
judgement.news_note: News flow is dominated by a well-corroborated 5% commercial workforce cut and production/delivery weakness, with the band-driving "more layoffs possible" headline resting on a single, body-less Reuters report amid otherwise strong positive order news.
lifts_it: Score falling 7.8 points to below 20 (Healthy threshold)
Negative layoff/production news aging out without fresh escalation (365-day half-life)
Independent corroboration that no further layoffs are planned, reversing the latest headline's implication
worsens_it: Score rising 22.2 points to 50 (High Risk threshold)
Payment slipping to 33 days past due, which alone would reach the next band
Further corroborated layoff, delivery-decline or production-delay news extending the current pattern
